translations.text: Before dawn the noble-born women began to make ready to go. The company of men knew that the prince's body was enclosed in the tomb.

The weary women meant to lament the prince's death with weeping for a while, to mourn him sorrowfully. The resting-place had grown cold, the departure had been hard; the warriors whom they found joyful at the tomb were brave in spirit.
Mary came at daybreak, mourning, and told another woman to come with her, a nobleman's daughter.
The two sorrowful women went looking for God's victorious Son, who lay alone in the tomb, where they knew that the men of the Jews had hidden him.
They thought that he would have to stay in the grave mound, alone on that Easter night. But the women knew something else about this by the time they turned away!
Before dawn, though, a troop of angels came there. The joy of the heavenly hosts surrounded the Saviour's tomb.
The tomb was open. The prince's body received the spirit of life, the earth shook, and those in hell laughed. The young warrior woke, brave, from the earth. The Majesty rose, victorious and wise.
John, a hero among those in hell, spoke. Laughing and brave, he spoke to the crowd about his kinsman's [?]:
"Our Saviour, the lord of all people, promised me when he was about to send me on this journey that he would come looking for me in six months. Now [?] has passed.
I fully expect, and I am certain, that today the Lord, God's victorious Son, will come looking for [us].
Then the Lord of mankind hurried on his journey; the Protector of the heavens, fiercest of all kings, meant to break down and lay low the walls of hell and begin to plunder the might of that city.

He cared nothing for a battle with helmeted warriors, and he did not intend to lead men in mail coats to the city gates. Instead the locks and the bars fell from the fortresses. The king rode in. The lord of all people, who gives glory to the hosts, hurried forward.
The exiles crowded forward, each wanting to be the one who might see the victorious Son: Adam and Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, many a brave nobleman, Moses and David,
Isaiah and Zacharias, many patriarchs, and also a gathering of men, a host of prophets, a crowd of women, many virgins, and countless people.
Then John saw God's victorious Son coming to hell in royal majesty. Sad in mind, he then understood that this was the coming of God himself.
He saw the doors of hell shining brightly, doors that had long been locked and covered in darkness. The servant was filled with joy.
Then the leader of the city's inhabitants spoke out boldly, brave before the crowd. He spoke to his kinsman and greeted the welcome visitor with words:
"Thanks be to you, our Lord, that you were willing to come looking for us [?], now that we in these bonds [?] wait. When many people bind a brotherless exile

(he is an outlaw far and wide), he is never so tightly held under the enemy's lock, so harshly bound in cruel fetters, that he cannot take courage more easily when he trusts that his lord's favour will make him want to ransom him from those bonds.
In the same way, all of us trust in you alone, my dear Lord. I have endured much since you came in to me [?], when you gave me a sword and a mail coat,
a helmet and battle gear (I have kept them always, until now), and you made known to me, joy of royal majesty, that you would be a protector to my people.
O Gabriel, how wise and sharp you are, gentle and mindful and meek, wise in your understanding and prudent in your words!

You made that known when you brought the boy to us in Bethlehem. We waited a long time for this. We sat in sorrow, longing for peace, in joy and hope, waiting for the time when we would hear the word of God spoken by his own mouth.
O Mary, how mighty a king you bore for us when you brought that child to us in Bethlehem! Trembling at this, we had to wait in hardship, in bonds, beneath the doors of hell.
The slayer rejoiced in his work. Our ancient enemies were all happy when they heard how we grieved and mourned our kindred, until the victorious Lord God [?] of all kings.
Now [?] gave us [?] from our youth. Through greedy minds we deceived ourselves. Because of that we carry those sins in our hearts into the slayer's hands, and we must even beg our enemies for peace.
O Jerusalem in Judea, how still you have stayed in that place!
Not all living people on earth who sing praise were allowed to travel through you.
You can encompass all the dwelling-places of the peoples; likewise, mighty Lord, best of all kings, you can count the grains of sand in the sea.
[?] hand, when you, Lord of hosts, chose by your own power to seek us on this journey of exile, and before Jerusalem in Judea,
(that city must nevertheless now wait, dear prince, for your return), and by the Jordan in Judea (we two bathed together in that stream).

With that water, Lord of hosts, you joyfully sprinkled all the city-dwellers, just as you and John in the Jordan, with that baptism, beautifully inspired this whole world. For that let there always be thanks to the Lord!"
